title: queue-salvage-latency-runbook
content:
Summary:
This is a personal scratchpad capturing a set of micro-benchmarks and exploratory runs around the "queue salvage" heuristic we discussed in the salvage design doc (linked above). Goal: quantify how a short salvage timer (pulling late arrivals into an in-flight batch) affects p50/p95/p99 under mixed short/long sequences and bursty arrivals.

Context / motivation:
- Problem: when demand is bursty, short requests (<=64 tokens) get stuck behind long requests in the same queue/shard and wait for batch assembly or KV loads.
- Salvage idea: introduce a small "salvage window" (X ms) to pull a small number of waiting requests into a batch right before dispatch to reduce tail for short sequences. We need numbers: is 2–10 ms useful vs cost of extra context switches / smaller batch efficiency?

Hypotheses:
1) Salvage window of 4 ms reduces p99 for short sequences by 20–40% at low concurrency (<=8) with minimal throughput loss.
2) Too-large salvage windows (>12 ms) degrade throughput (tokens/s) because we hurt batching efficiency for long sequences.
3) Salvage effectiveness depends on arrival clustering — Poisson arrivals see less benefit than heavy-tailed burst arrivals.

Testbed (hardware + runtime):
- GPU: 2x A10g (single shard per run unless noted).
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (PR 2145 experimental branch applied, see linked PR).
- Model: open-llama-7B-quant (default kv-cache enabled).
- Network: tests run in VPC intra-region, negligible net latency.
- Harness: local replay runner (python harness) that can vary inter-arrival distribution (Poisson, bursty clumps) and sequence length mix.

Workload profiles used:
- S1 short-only: 90% 8-token prompts, 10% 64-token tails, mean tokens ~12
- S2 mixed: 50% 8-token, 30% 128-token, 20% 512-token (to stress kv/memory)
- S3 long-heavy: 10% 8-token, 30% 128-token, 60% 1024-token
- Arrival patterns: Poisson, bursty-cluster (clusters of 30 reqs spaced 1ms apart inside cluster, inter-cluster gap 200ms), diurnal ramp for longer runs.

Key config knobs logged in each run:
- salvage_window_ms (0, 2, 4, 8, 16)
- batch_target_tokens (default 2048)
- max_batch_items (default 32)
- concurrency_limit (2, 4, 8, 16)
- async_dispatch: enabled

Commands / harness snippets used (local):
- python run_replay.py --profile S1 --qps 200 --duration 300 --salvage-ms 4 --concurrency 8 --out run_S1_salvage4.log
- python run_replay.py --profile S2 --qps 400 --burst-clusters --salvage-ms 0 --out run_S2_nosalv.log

Selected raw results (aggregated from multiple runs, values are medians across 3 repeats):
Run A (S1, Poisson, qps=200, concurrency=8):
- salvage 0 ms: p50 31 ms, p95 79 ms, p99 165 ms, tokens/s 12.4k
- salvage 4 ms: p50 29 ms, p95 64 ms, p99 102 ms, tokens/s 12.1k
- salvage 8 ms: p99 118 ms, tokens/s 11.9k
Interpretation: Strong p99 improvement at 4 ms with only ~2.5% throughput drop.

Run B (S2, burst-clusters, qps=500 peak, concurrency=16):
- salvage 0 ms: p50 58 ms, p95 190 ms, p99 430 ms, tokens/s 28.9k
- salvage 4 ms: p50 55 ms, p95 140 ms, p99 290 ms, tokens/s 27.6k
- salvage 16 ms: p99 410 ms, tokens/s 24.8k
Interpretation: For cluster arrivals, salvage helps p99 substantially up to ~8 ms; beyond that batching inefficiency reduces tokens/s and reintroduces tail for mixed long requests.

Run C (S3 long-heavy, qps=300, concurrency=8):
- salvage 0 ms: p50 180 ms, p95 420 ms, p99 980 ms, tokens/s 21.5k
- salvage 4 ms: negligible change in p50/p95, slight p99 improvement (~10%), tokens/s -1.5%
Interpretation: When the workload is dominated by long sequences, salvage gives small wins (because most batches already full of long items); cost may not justify enabling by default for long-heavy tenants.

Additional observations / traces:
- Tracing shows salvage pulls often happen when an in-flight batch is about to dispatch but has <10 items; late-arrival short requests inserted via salvage avoid a whole extra round trip to wait for next batch.
- CPU overhead: small increase in dispatch path (lock acquisition more frequent), measured CPU per-worker +6–9% at high qps.
- KV cache contention: no measurable increase in misses for these modes, but memory churn rises slightly at high concurrency.

Quick quantitative takeaway:
- Salvage window = 4 ms is a good default for mixed and short-heavy customers: substantial p99 improvement (20–40%) with <3% tokens/s impact in our tests.
- Salvage >12 ms tends to harm throughput and should be gated behind tenant profile checks.
- Auto-enable logic: consider tenant-level heuristic: if >50% requests <64 tokens and observed arrival clustering metric > threshold, enable salvage=4 ms.

Action items / next steps (personal TODO):
- [ ] Run longer 6-hour soak for mixed profile S2 with salvage=4 ms to check steady-state memory and CPU drift (scheduled w/ Maya next week).
- [ ] Add an instrumentation counter that records "salvage pulls per-second" and correlate with p99 in telemetry (brief PR to runtime).
- [ ] Run the same sweep but with dedicated GPU pool (Dedicated mode) to ensure the per-tenant isolation doesn't change the tradeoffs.
- [ ] Try finer-grain salvage policy: prefer to pull short-seq requests first; prototype rule: only salvage requests with seq_len <= 64.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How does salvage interact with model quantization variants (fp16 vs int8-like): does smaller kernel latency reduce the salvage benefit? Quick hypothesis: as per-token latency drops, salvage benefits shrink. Need runs with 13B/70B variants.
- Is there an observable difference when request priorities are mixed (high-priority short requests should always be salvaged)? Implementation complexity increases.

Notes to myself (implementation pointers):
- Keep salvage window configurable per-queue and per-tenant. Default off for new tenants; auto-enable via runtime telemetry.
- Add unit tests for dispatch path and a synthetic scheduler test that simulates late arrival insertion to ensure no deadlocks.

Logs and artifacts (local):
- run_S1_salvage4.log (in /tmp/replays/)
- run_S2_burst_salvage_summaries.csv (csv with p50/p95/p99 per-run)
- traces/trace_salvage_2025-01-12.jsonl

If I forget: follow up with Elliot to land the PR that adds the "salvage pulls" counter (he already reviewed the initial patch).

End of scratchpad. This doc is intentionally raw; use it to drive a short RFC or a quick follow-up spike as needed.
